peer_results.rationale: AMD's candidates focus on hardware platforms (FPGAs/Adaptive SoCs) and hyperscale customer infrastructure, lacking substantive overlap with AVGO's specific topic of 'Private AI' services that bring the model to customer data to ensure privacy and control.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel views AI as a generational shift and aims to bring AI to where data is generated and used, addressing the full AI continuum from GenAI to AI PCs and edge computing. The company leverages a spectrum of hardware and software platforms for open, modular solutions and is infusing AI into its technologies to support current and future workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and INTC emphasize bringing AI services and infrastructure directly to where the data resides to address privacy and control concerns, though they focus on different layers of the stack. AVGO offers 'Private AI' services that bring the AI model to the customer's data to ensure privacy and compliance, while INTC's strategy is explicitly to 'bring AI to where the data is being generated and used' across the full AI continuum, including edge and cloud.

sentences.text: Advanced services for Private AI provide customers with the benefits of AI without having to compromise control of data, privacy, and compliance by bringing the AI model to customers' data.
Our strategy is to bring AI to where the data is being generated and used.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center AI and High-Performance Storage Offerings
comparisons.peer_summary: Demand for AI and big data is driving the need for high-performance storage; SBU addresses this with the 6500 30TB SSD for AI data lakes and sampled the 9550 series in 2024 for AI and high-performance computing workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU highlight the specific demand for high-performance infrastructure to support AI workloads, particularly in the context of data lakes and big data analytics. AVGO's Private AI services help customers manage AI data without compromising privacy, while MU's 6500 SSDs are explicitly designed with high performance and endurance for 'AI data lake applications,' reflecting the shared need for robust data handling in AI environments.

peer_results.rationale: NVDA's candidate D055 discusses general regulatory compliance risks rather than AI service architecture, and candidate D002 describes a general full-stack software solution (CUDA) for accelerating computing, which is a different technical approach and topic from AVGO's specific 'Private AI' service model focused on data locality and compliance.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm believes generative AI use cases must run on-device to maximize utility by bringing immediacy, privacy, security, and personalization benefits to consumers.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and QCOM share a focus on privacy and security as key drivers for AI deployment strategies, though they apply them to different segments. AVGO brings the AI model to the customer's data to 'compromise control of data, privacy, and compliance,' while QCOM argues that generative AI must run 'on-device to maximize utility, and bring the benefits of immediacy, privacy, security and personalization,' aligning on privacy as a critical technical and business requirement for AI.

sentences.text: Advanced services for Private AI provide customers with the benefits of AI without having to compromise control of data, privacy, and compliance by bringing the AI model to customers' data.

While these generative AI models are developed primarily for use in the cloud, we believe that the variety of innovative enterprise and consumer use cases that have emerged and will continue to emerge from generative AI must run on-device to maximize their utility, and bring the benefits of immediacy, privacy, security and personalization to consumers.
